subject: Microbiology
subtopic: Rickettsial Typhus Fevers: organism, transmission, pathogenesis, clinical features, diagnosis, treatment and prevention
concept: Rickettsial typhus includes epidemic typhus caused by Rickettsia prowazekii, flea-borne typhus caused by R. typhi, and scrub typhus caused by Orientia tsutsugamushi. Vector exposure and intracellular endothelial infection are central to disease.

content.definition: Rickettsial typhus includes epidemic typhus caused by Rickettsia prowazekii, flea-borne typhus caused by R. typhi, and scrub typhus caused by Orientia tsutsugamushi. Vector exposure and intracellular endothelial infection are central to disease.

content.mechanism: The pathogen's tissue tropism, replication or intracellular persistence explains the characteristic clinical syndrome.
content.structure: Organism-specific structural and biologic features are summarized in the concept and high-yield fields.
content.function: Biologic properties determine transmission and tissue injury.
effects: severe systemic, pulmonary or neurologic disease is possible
content.clinical_relevance: Rickettsial Typhus Fevers is an official Hematology microbiology syllabus topic.
content.diagnosis: Diagnosis uses compatible illness/exposure with PCR or paired serology when available. Doxycycline should not be delayed when clinical suspicion is strong.
content.treatment: Treatment is clinical-context dependent and should follow current local/international guidance; supportive care and management of complications are important where applicable.
